sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AS THE MID-LEVEL TROUGH OVER ERN NOAM SHIFTS SLOWLY EWD...SOME SLIGHT DEAMPLIFICATION OF THE FLOW FIELD ACROSS THE CONUS IS EXPECTED...WITH FLOW TRENDING A BIT MORE ZONAL WITH TIME. A MAIN FEATURE ALOFT IN TERMS OF CONVECTIVE WEATHER WILL BE A COMPLEX SHORT-WAVE TROUGH CROSSING THE NRN INTERMOUNTAIN REGION AND SPREADING INTO THE DAKOTAS/NEB DURING THE AFTERNOON. AT THE SURFACE...LEE TROUGHING WILL PERSIST OVER THE HIGH PLAINS...WHILE THE MAIN SURFACE BAROCLINIC ZONE SHIFTS SWD AND THEN STALLS ACROSS N TX AND EWD INTO THE GULF COAST STATES.

sections.title: NRN AND CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: WITH HEATING/DESTABILIZATION OF THE AIRMASS ACROSS THE PLAINS FORECAST DURING THE AFTERNOON...INITIAL PIECE OF THE SHORT-WAVE TROUGH SHIFTING EWD ACROSS THE NRN INTERMOUNTAIN REGION WILL BEGIN AFFECTING THE HIGH PLAINS AND INTO THE WRN DAKOTAS/WRN NEB. THIS SHOULD RESULT IN EVENTUAL CONVECTIVE INITIATION -- POSSIBLY ACROSS THE HIGH PLAINS OF MT AND VICINITY INITIALLY...BUT THEN EWD INTO SRN ND/SD AND EVENTUALLY NEB. WITH 40 TO 50 KT WLYS ACCOMPANYING THE MID-LEVEL SYSTEM SPREADING ATOP LOW-LEVEL SLYS...SHEAR WILL BECOME INCREASINGLY SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS -- PARTICULARLY INTO THE EVENING AS THE LOW-LEVEL JET INTENSIFIES. AS A RESULT...DEVELOPING STORMS SHOULD ORGANIZE/ACQUIRE ROTATION...AND GIVEN DEGREE OF INSTABILITY EXPECTED...LARGE HAIL IS LIKELY ALONG WITH ISOLATED DAMAGING WINDS. A COUPLE OF TORNADOES MAY ALSO OCCUR DEPENDING UPON STORM MODE...THOUGH INDICATIONS ARE THAT STORMS SHOULD EVOLVE INTO CLUSTERS/ONE OR MORE MCS...WHICH WOULD LIKELY YIELD GREATER WIND THREAT BUT A LESSER POTENTIAL FOR TORNADOES. AS THE LOW-LEVEL JET INCREASES FROM THE SOUTH DURING THE EVENING...UPSCALE-GROWING STORMS SHOULD TURN SSEWD...CROSSING NEB AND SERN SD DURING THE OVERNIGHT HOURS.

sections.title: OK AND VICINITY EWD INTO THE MID MS VALLEY AREA
sections.text: ONGOING CONVECTION FORECAST ACROSS PORTIONS OF OK/AR WILL COMPLICATE THE FORECAST IN TERMS OF THE DETAILS OF EVOLUTION. IN GENERAL HOWEVER...EXPECT AN INCREASE IN AFTERNOON CONVECTION NEAR AND N OF THE SURFACE FRONT AS HEATING/DESTABILIZATION OCCURS AWAY FROM LINGERING CLOUDS/CONVECTION. DESPITE MODEST MID-LEVEL FLOW...ELY COMPONENT TO THE LOW LEVEL FLOW ON THE COOL SIDE OF THE FRONT SHOULD ENHANCE SHEAR SUFFICIENTLY TO SUPPORT MULTICELL SEVERE STORMS. THEREFORE...WILL MAINTAIN SLIGHT RISK FOR HAIL/WIND ACROSS THIS CORRIDOR. ..GOSS/LEITMAN.. 08/11/2011

sections.title: NRN/CENTRAL PLAINS AREA THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: A MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER THE NRN ROCKIES WILL PROGRESS EWD TO THE NRN HIGH PLAINS TONIGHT...AND THIS WAVE WILL BE PRECEDED BY SMALLER-SCALE EMBEDDED SPEED MAXIMA MOVING EWD/ENEWD FROM THE NRN GREAT BASIN. LEE CYCLOGENESIS WILL OCCUR ACROSS THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS...WHICH WILL HELP DRAW RESIDUAL BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS IN THE LOW 60S NWD FROM NEB/KS TO THE DAKOTAS...BENEATH A PLUME OF 7-8 C/KM MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES. THE INCREASING MOISTURE AND LAPSE RATES WILL COMBINE WITH DAYTIME HEATING TO RESULT IN AFTERNOON MLCAPE VALUES OF 1500-2500 J/KG. SOME CLOUDS/CONVECTION WILL SPREAD EWD FROM ERN MT TO ND IN ASSOCIATION WITH A LEAD SHORTWAVE TROUGH. THE MORE SUBSTANTIAL THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED BY MID-LATE AFTERNOON INVOF THE ND/SD/MT BORDER AS SURFACE HEATING AND LOW-LEVEL ASCENT WEAKEN THE CAP...AND THE NRN ROCKIES TROUGH APPROACHES FROM THE W. THE MODERATE INSTABILITY IN THE WARM SECTOR WILL COINCIDE WITH SUFFICIENT DEEP-LAYER SHEAR FOR SUPERCELLS AS THE 40 KT WLY MIDLEVEL FLOW OVERLAYS SLY LOW-LEVEL WINDS. THE NET RESULT WILL BE AN ENVIRONMENT SUPPORTIVE OF SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING VERY LARGE HAIL AND DAMAGING WINDS. THE TORNADO THREAT IS A LITTLE MORE UNCER

sections.title: SRN PLAINS TO LOWER MS VALLEY TODAY
sections.text: SEVERAL CLUSTERS OF THUNDERSTORMS ARE ONGOING THIS MORNING FROM NW MS WNWWD TO NW OK. THIS CONVECTION HAS BEEN FOCUSED NEAR AND N OF A SURFACE FRONT ACROSS NRN MS/SRN AR AND THE RED RIVER VALLEY...WITH LOW-LEVEL WAA THE PRIMARY SUPPORTING FACTOR. THE IMPACT OF THE RELATIVELY WIDESPREAD CONVECTION ON DAYTIME HEATING IS SOMEWHAT UNCERTAIN...THOUGH THE STORM CLUSTERS SHOULD TEND TO WEAKEN LATER THIS MORNING AND WAA AND LOW-LEVEL FLOW DIMINISH. THAT SUGGESTS THAT THE ISOLATED SEVERE THREAT THIS AFTERNOON WILL BE FOCUSED ALONG THE OUTFLOW-REINFORCED FRONT FROM CENTRAL MS TO THE RED RIVER VALLEY...WHERE STRONG SURFACE HEATING S OF THE BOUNDARY WILL SUPPORT STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND SOME DOWNBURST POTENTIAL. SIMILAR TO THE PAST TWO NIGHTS...THE THREAT FOR ELEVATED THUNDERSTORMS WILL INCREASE ACROSS OK AS A SLY LLJ DEVELOPS...COINCIDENT WITH THE EWD PROGRESS OF ANY REMNANT CLUSTERS ALONG THE SURFACE FRONT ACROSS NW TX. ..THOMPSON/ROGERS.. 08/11/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER THE NRN/CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS FROM THE SRN PLAINS INTO THE LOWER MS VALLEY...

sections.title: NRN/CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY INDICATES THE PRIMARY UPPER TROUGH/VORTICITY MAX OVER NWRN MT MOVING EWD TOWARD THE NRN HIGH PLAINS...WITH A DOWNSTREAM WEAKER SHORT WAVE TROUGH MOVING ACROSS SERN MT TOWARD THE DAKOTAS AT THIS TIME. FARTHER SOUTH...ADDITIONAL LOW AMPLITUDE PERTURBATIONS ARE EVIDENT OVER THE NEB PANHANDLE AND NERN UT/SWRN WY...EMBEDDED WITHIN THE STRONGER WNWLY FLOW ALOFT. THESE FEATURES ARE EXPECTED TO IMPACT THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON AND TONIGHT AS MOISTURE INCREASES NWD OVER THE REGION IN ASSOCIATION WITH WEAK PRESSURE FALLS OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS. 12Z REGIONAL SOUNDINGS EXHIBITED STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES OVER THE NRN ROCKIES/HIGH PLAINS...AND WHEN COMBINED WITH INCREASING LOW LEVEL MOISTURE AND STRONG DIABATIC HEATING...WILL RESULT IN MLCAPE OF 1500-2500 J/KG. THE HEATING COUPLED WITH WEAK LARGE SCALE ASCENT WILL GRADUALLY WEAKEN THE CAP WITH CONVECTION INCREASING DURING THE MID-LATE AFTERNOON FROM SERN MT/SWRN ND INTO WRN/CENTRAL SD. WINDS ARE FORECAST TO VEER AND INCREASE WITH HEIGHT WITH 40-50 KT OF DEEP LAYER SHEAR EXPECTED OVER THE AREA IN ASSOCIATION WITH THE STRONGER BAND OF WNWLY MID/UPPER LEVEL FLOW. THIS WILL ENHANCE STORM ORGANIZATION AND INTENS

sections.title: SRN PLAINS/LOWER MS VALLEY
sections.text: MULTIPLE MCS/S FROM OK AND AR INTO MS/AL HAVE REINFORCED A SERIES OF CONVECTIVE OUTFLOWS AND FORCED THE EFFECTIVE SURFACE BOUNDARY SWD ACROSS SRN OK...NERN TX...NRN/CENTRAL LA...AND SRN PARTS OF MS/AL. STORM CLUSTERS OCCURRING NORTH OF THESE BOUNDARIES ARE LARGELY ELEVATED...OCCURRING WITHIN AN ENVIRONMENT CHARACTERIZED BY STEEP MID LEVEL LAPSE RATES BUT WEAKENING WINDS ALOFT/VERTICAL SHEAR WITH SWD EXTENT. THE QLCS MOVING EWD ACROSS CENTRAL/SRN OK HAS CONTINUED TO BUILD SWD TO THE RED RIVER...AND STRONG HEATING DOWNSTREAM FROM THE SYSTEM OVER NORTH CENTRAL/NERN TX INTO SERN OK SHOULD PROMOTE CONTINUED DESTABILIZATION. THE STEEP LAPSE RATES WILL BE SUPPORTIVE OF HAIL IN STRONGER STORMS...AND WET MICROBURST POTENTIAL MAY INCREASE FOR STORMS CLOSER TO THE EFFECTIVE SURFACE BOUNDARY THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING. ..WEISS/HURLBUT.. 08/11/2011

sections.title: THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS IN THE ARKLATEX
sections.text: ...THERE IS A SLGT RISK OF SVR TSTMS PORTIONS OF EAST CENTRAL NM EWD INTO FAR SWRN OK...

sections.title: SRN PLAINS AND ARKLATEX AREA
sections.text: MCS WITH STRONG MESO-HIGH HAS CONTINUED TO PROGRESS EWD THROUGH THE DAY. LEADING EDGE OF SYSTEM AT 1930 UTC EXTENDED FROM NEAR FSM SWWD INTO FAR SERN ERN OK...AND THEN WSWWD INTO NRN/WRN TX. STRONG OVERTURNING OF AIR MASS AND RESULTANT COOL/STABILIZED BOUNDARY LAYER WILL INHIBIT REDEVELOPMENT OF SURFACE BASED DEVELOPMENT ACROSS MUCH OF OK. PRESENCE OF ORGANIZED LINE/COLD POOL ACROSS FAR SERN OK IS EXPECTED TO PERSIST FOR THE NEXT FEW HOURS. THIS SYSTEM...OR AT LEAST THE STRONGER ACTIVITY...IS EXPECTED TO TURN MORE SSEWD TOWARD SHV...ALONG A REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM CONVECTION EARLIER THIS MORNING. HOWEVER...THE SEVERE THREAT SHOULD NOT EXTEND TOO MUCH SOUTH OF SHV AS THE STORMS MOVE INTO WEAKER FLOW ALOFT. STORMS HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED ACROSS FAR WRN TX AND ERN NM. WITHIN WSWLY FLOW ALOFT...THESE STORMS SHOULD SPREAD NEWD TOWARD/INTO THE TX PANHANDLE. THE PRESENCE OF MODERATE INSTABILITY AND THE STRONGLY VEERING WIND PROFILES...NORTH OF THE BOUNDARY... SHOULD SUPPORT A FEW SEVERE MULTICELLS WITH HAIL AND WIND.

sections.title: NRN/CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: FORECAST GENERALLY ON TRACK AS MAIN LARGE SCALE FORCING SHIFTS EWD FROM THE NRN ROCKIES INTO THE NRN/CENTRAL PLAINS LATER TODAY AND TONIGHT. HOWEVER...LOWERED THE SEVERE PROBABILITIES ACROSS NERN KS AS LARGE SCALE FORCING AND LOW LEVEL WARM ADVECTION REMAIN NORTH AND WEST OF THE AREA OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: SERN STATES
sections.text: A FEW CLUSTERS OF STORMS SHOULD PERSIST INTO THE EVENING HOURS ACROSS THE SERN STATES. THERE IS ENOUGH MID LEVEL FLOW FOR WEAK STORM ORGANIZATION...AND STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES FAVOR A FEW STORMS WITH MARGINAL WIND DAMAGE. HOWEVER...THE THREAT IS NOT ANTICIPATED TO BE WIDESPREAD ENOUGH TO SUPPORT A SLIGHT RISK. ..IMY.. 08/11/2011 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1124 AM CDT THU AUG 11 2011/

sections.title: CNTRL PLAINS
sections.text: EARLY EVENING MATURE QLCS WAS MOVING ROUGHLY 290/35KT ACROSS SERN SD. FCST PROPAGATION VECTORS SUGGEST NO SUBSTANTIAL CHANGE IN MOTION OVERNIGHT WITH PREFERENTIAL/BACKBUILDING DEVELOPMENT ALONG LLVL THETA-E GRADIENT IN CNTRL/NERN NEB OVERNIGHT. FORWARD-FLANK SHOULD TRACK ESE INTO FAR SWRN MN/NWRN IA...WITH A WEAKENING TREND WITH EWD EXTENT OWING TO MORE STABLE ENVIRONMENT. SWRN EXTENT OF ACTIVITY MAY EVENTUALLY BECOME THE STRONGEST OF STORMS AND LIKELY REMAIN NEAR OR ENTIRELY SFC-BASED. MID-LVL WNW FLOW OF 35-40 KTS COUPLED WITH AN INCREASING SLY LLJ WILL LIKELY INSTIGATE OCCASIONAL BOWING STRUCTURES CAPABLE OF HIGH WINDS. ACTIVITY WILL LIKELY ADVANCE AS FAR SE AS FAR NW MO/NERN KS BY 12Z.

sections.title: NRN HIGH PLAINS
sections.text: PRIMARY UPR TROUGH /H5 TEMP AOB MINUS 15 DEG C/ CONTINUES TO MOVE EWD ACROSS CNTRL MT THIS EVENING. TSTMS THAT DEVELOPED ALONG THE HIGHER TERRAIN AND THE LEE TROUGH HAVE BEEN THRIVING IN A MODESTLY UNSTABLE AIR MASS /MLCAPES TO 1500 J PER KG/ AND 40 KTS OF WLY DEEP-LAYER SHEAR. SFC ANALYSIS SHOWS THAT THE AIR MASS MADE A LATE AFTN RECOVERY IN A NARROW ZONE FROM W OF THE SD BLACK HILLS NWD INTO SERN MT/SWRN ND. MATURE STORMS WILL LIKELY SURVIVE A WHILE LONGER INTO THIS ZONE WITH THREATS FOR LARGE HAIL AND HIGH WINDS...BUT THEN WEAKEN FARTHER E WHERE STRONGER MLCINH/MORE STABILITY EXISTS ON THE LOWER PLAINS. ..RACY.. 08/12/2011
